title: Fonctions L / Équation fonctionnelle des fonctions L (cas géométrique) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. The page belongs to Grothendieck's notes on the functional equation of L-functions of l-adic sheaves on a curve X over a finite field (the SGA 5 circle of ideas). η is the generic point, E_η is an l-adic representation of the generic Galois group, and E_η^♮ is some canonical extension of E_η to X, very plausibly the direct image j_*E_η, whose stalk at a closed point x is the inertia invariants E_η^{I_x}. Everything is computed in a Grothendieck group: either of constructible sheaves on X, or of Galois modules of the residue fields k(x) pushed forward by f_{x*} from x to X.

Definitions. For each closed point x the page sets α_x(E_η) = E_η^{♮(x)} − E_η(x). Read literally, this is the virtual difference between the stalk of the extension at x and a 'generic' term E_η(x); the latter is not defined on this page. It then sets μ_x(E) = α_x(E_η)^∨ − α_x(Ě_η)(1).

Symmetry check (bracketed aside). Grothendieck verifies μ_x(Ě) = −μ_x(E)^∨(1), and equivalently μ_x(E) = −μ_x(Ě)^∨(1). This is immediate from the definition, using double dual = identity and the rule (A(1))^∨ = A^∨(−1). A first attempt at this line, of the form μ_x(Ě) = μ_x..., is struck out.

Main formula (boxed). The duality formula on the class of E^♮ in K_0 reads D(E_η^♮) = Ě_η^♮(1) + Σ_{x∈X^{(0)}} f_{x*}(μ_x(E)). So the dualizing functor D (Verdier duality, with the shift absorbed into the K-group sign conventions) sends the canonical extension of E to the canonical extension of the dual Tate twist, up to point-supported corrections μ_x.

Additivity remark (NB). α_x is not additive in E_η, because invariants are not exact, but μ_x is. This fits the identity Ě^{I} = (E_I)^∨: the dual of the invariants of Ě is the coinvariants of E, and the combination invariants minus coinvariants is an Euler characteristic of inertia cohomology, hence additive. For the tame part one has H^1(I,E) ≅ E_I(−1).

Self-dual case. If Ě_η ≅ E_η(φ) for a twist φ, the formula specialises to D(E^♮) = E^♮(φ+1) + Σ f_{x*}μ_x(E), with μ_x(E) = α_x(E_η)^∨ − α_x(E_η)(φ+1). This is the shape needed for a functional equation relating L(X,E,t) to L(X,E,1/(q^{?}t)) with explicit local correction factors at the bad points.

Purpose. Through the Grothendieck–Lefschetz trace formula and the compatibility of duality with Frobenius traces, the K-group formula yields the functional equation of L(X,E). The local correction factors are given by the μ_x.
errors: E_η(x) in the definition of α_x is not defined on the page, so the meaning of α_x as written is not self-contained. It presumably denotes a generic-rank or virtual term, or the restriction of E_η to the decomposition group at x, defined on an earlier page. Signs and shifts of D in K_0 are left implicit.
The struck-out line '[μ_x(Ě) = μ_x ...]' was an aborted attempt, corrected immediately afterwards. No substantive error is visible in the symmetry computation.

ideas.what: Duality for the canonical (j_*) extension of a generic l-adic representation on a curve, computed in K_0 with point-supported local correction terms
ideas.modern_name: Verdier duality for middle/direct-image extensions on curves; local terms in the functional equation of L-functions
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (SGA 5, functional equation of L-functions, 1965–66); Deligne (SGA 4½)
ideas.where_published: SGA 5 (exposés on L-functions, as written up by others; Grothendieck's own functional-equation exposé was not published in final form)

ideas.what: Local invariant μ_x built from invariants minus 'coinvariants', additive even though invariants are not
ideas.modern_name: Euler characteristic of inertia cohomology; local L-factor corrections (relatives of the Artin/Swan conductor data)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck, Serre (Euler–Poincaré characteristic formulas), Raynaud (Bourbaki exposé on Grothendieck–Ogg–Shafarevich)

ideas.what: Symmetry μ_x(Ě) = −μ_x(E)^∨(1) and specialisation to the self-dual-up-to-twist case
ideas.modern_name: Self-duality of local factors / functional equation of an orthogonal or symplectic local system

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful but routine K-group bookkeeping of duality for j_* extensions on a curve, aimed at the functional equation of L-functions. The material belongs to the SGA 5 programme, which is well documented (though partly unpublished by Grothendieck himself). Nothing here goes beyond what Deligne and others later wrote up; epsilon factors and product formulas do not appear on this page.
transcription_corrections: The struck-out line '[-μ_x(Ě)=μ_x-]' is a crossed-out partial formula ('μ_x(Ě) = μ_x'), not a statement.
In the bracketed aside, the stray '}' after 'α_x(E_η)(1)' is a closing parenthesis in the manuscript. The aside begins with 'donc' and ends with 'i.e.'.
The superscript written as ♮ may be a handwritten symbol for the canonical extension (plausibly j_*); its rendering as ♮ is uncertain.
'μ_x(E_η) l'est' in the NB: Grothendieck writes μ_x(E_η), consistent with μ_x being additive in E_η.
